question: What is the absolute first action a nurse expects when caring for a patient with serum sickness?

options.A: Stop administering the triggering medication
options.B: Start immediate daily kidney dialysis
options.C: Give a blood transfusion to replace red cells
options.D: Apply cool water compresses to the joints

explanation: Rule number one in pharmacology reactions: stop the offending drug immediately so no more immune complexes can form! [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of vasopressor medications in treating shock?

options.A: To dissolve dangerous blood clots in the lungs
options.B: To constrict blood vessels and raise blood pressure
options.C: To slow down a dangerously rapid heart rate
options.D: To fight off severe bacterial infections

explanation: Vasopressors work by tightening smooth muscles in the blood vessels, increasing vascular resistance and blood pressure. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the main job of nutrition in the human body?

options.A: Eliminating the need for physical exercise
options.B: Providing energy and building blocks for repair
options.C: Increasing overall body temperature constantly
options.D: Preventing all known genetic disorders

explanation: Spot on! Food gives our bodies the fuel we need to move around, stay alive, and heal when we get hurt. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h1)

question: A nurse wants to search for articles mentioning either 'pain' or 'discomfort'. Which search word should be used?

options.A: NOT
options.B: AND
options.C: WITH
options.D: OR

explanation: The word OR tells the database to look for either term, helping you catch helpful synonyms and expand your search. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology?

options.A: The chemical composition of human blood
options.B: The electrical signals of the nervous system
options.C: The study of microscopic living organisms
options.D: The physical structure of human bones

explanation: Microbiology specifically investigates organisms too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye. [learn more](GST114_U1_T1#GST114_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the best way to start talking to a patient who has a hearing impairment?

options.A: Stand behind the patient and speak loudly to surprise them into listening
options.B: Turn on the television to provide background noise for a normal atmosphere
options.C: Get the patient's attention visually and face them directly before speaking
options.D: Keep the room dark so the patient can concentrate entirely on sound

explanation: You're a natural! Facing them and getting their attention first lets them use your facial expressions and lip movements to understand you better. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h5)

question: Which action best shows you are advocating for your patient at the end of life?

options.A: Withholding pain medication to keep the patient awake for visiting relatives
options.B: Ignoring advance directives if the attending physician disagrees with them
options.C: Ensuring a documented DNR order is followed despite objections from distant relatives
options.D: Following the loudest family member's demand to start aggressive CPR

explanation: As a nurse, your duty is to protect the patient's documented wishes, even when family members disagree. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T2#GNS221_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to ensure a health project is sustainable?

options.A: Involving village leaders in planning from the very beginning
options.B: Relying entirely on foreign staff to make every daily decision
options.C: Using affordable materials available within the local market
options.D: Training local residents as community health volunteers

explanation: Depending completely on outside staff creates dependency and guarantees the project will fail once those outsiders leave. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T10#GNS112_U5_T10_h6)

question: You are preparing a recovery bed for a patient coming back from theatre. Which item must you keep ready at the bedside?

options.A: An overhead exercise trapeze bar
options.B: Suction apparatus and emesis basin
options.C: Bedside dining tray and reading lamp
options.D: A heavy woolen floor rug and extra pillows

explanation: Great job! Patients waking up from anesthesia can easily choke on saliva or vomit, so having a suction machine and a basin nearby is a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: During an antenatal visit, how can a nurse best check a pregnant woman's nutritional status?

options.A: Give her a printed diet sheet in English without asking about her background
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about her usual daily meals and check her weight trend
options.C: Assume she eats well because she looks healthy on the outside
options.D: Wait until after delivery to discuss what kind of food she ate at home

explanation: Chatting warmly about what she actually eats daily and watching her weight trends helps you spot any nutritional gaps early and support her. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h7)

question: Why do nurses always warn patients with bleeding problems to stay away from everyday painkillers like ibuprofen?

options.A: NSAIDs increase blood pressure to dangerous levels and trigger acute strokes
options.B: NSAIDs instantly destroy all stored vitamin K reserves located inside the liver
options.C: NSAIDs negatively interfere with normal platelet aggregation and increase bleeding risks
options.D: NSAIDs cause the kidneys to stop producing red blood cells permanently

explanation: Medications like ibuprofen and aspirin get in the way of platelets sticking together, making it much harder for your body to stop any bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T11#GNS311_U2_T11_h8)

question: You are bagging an unresponsive patient with a bag-valve-mask, but their chest isn't rising. What should you do next?

options.A: Disconnect the oxygen tubing from the wall supply
options.B: Turn the patient onto their side in the recovery position
options.C: Squeeze the ventilation bag much harder and faster
options.D: Reposition the head and check the airway for blockage

explanation: If air isn't going in, don't just squeeze harder! Check for a blockage and readjust the head position to open up that airway properly. You're doing great. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T1#GNS112_U7_T1_h5)

question: Why are nurses considered frontline workers in infection surveillance?

options.A: They spend the most time observing patients at the bedside
options.B: They design the computer software used for hospital records
options.C: They are the only staff allowed to write public health laws
options.D: They fund all the laboratory testing in the facility

explanation: Bedside presence allows nurses to spot early signs of infection before anyone else. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is a primary reason nurseries have such strict sanitation and hand hygiene rules?

options.A: Parents demand that floors are polished with harsh chemicals daily
options.B: Young children easily spread germs by mouthing objects and touching surfaces
options.C: Local government sanitation laws prohibit the use of colorful toys
options.D: Infants are completely immune to all known bacterial infections

explanation: Toddlers frequently put objects in their mouths and touch everything around them, making strict hand hygiene essential to stop germs from spreading. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is a primary clinical feature of hemodynamic instability?

options.A: High fever with shivering and chills
options.B: Elevated urine output above normal limits
options.C: Gradual weight gain over several weeks
options.D: Inadequate blood flow to vital organs

explanation: Hemodynamic instability simply means the circulation is failing to supply enough blood to keep organs working properly. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h4)

question: Eighteen months after losing her husband, a widow still cannot leave her house, eat well, or talk about him without panicking. What kind of grief is she experiencing?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Complicated grief
options.C: Delayed grief
options.D: Normal grief

explanation: When grief stays extreme and stops someone from living their normal life long after a loss, we call it complicated grief. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h3)

question: A nurse uses a dietary assessment to establish a baseline. What does this mean for patient care?

options.A: It provides a starting point to measure future nutritional changes and treatment progress
options.B: It acts as a permanent record that cannot be altered during the hospital stay
options.C: It proves that the patient has no underlying metabolic diseases
options.D: It serves as the final clearance for the patient to be discharged home

explanation: Establishing a baseline gives healthcare providers a reference point to see if interventions are helping or if the patient's condition is worsening. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h2)

question: What is the main reason teenagers often avoid visiting standard healthcare clinics?

options.A: Lack of available transportation networks
options.B: Inability to swallow prescribed tablets
options.C: Preference for traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Fear of judgment and lack of privacy

explanation: Spot on! Teens worry about being scolded or having their personal business gossiped about, which keeps them away. Creating a safe space changes everything. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T12#GNS312_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which brain pathway is mainly responsible for positive symptoms of psychosis, like hearing voices or seeing things?

options.A: Mesocortical pathway
options.B: Mesolimbic pathway
options.C: Tuberoinfundibular pathway
options.D: Nigrostriatal pathway

explanation: When the mesolimbic pathway becomes hyperactive, it drives those 'positive' symptoms like hallucinations. That's why antipsychotics target this specific area! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h2)

question: Why is asking patients about their ability to afford basic needs important during a clinical assessment?

options.A: It proves whether the patient has a college degree
options.B: It guarantees immediate government financial grants
options.C: It helps uncover hidden financial strain affecting health
options.D: It replaces the need to check vital signs

explanation: Spot on! Many patients hide unemployment out of shame, so asking helps reveal financial stress that impacts their health and treatment. Well done! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h4)

question: Which part of the syringe driver securely holds the syringe plunger and pushes it forward?

options.A: The clear plastic needle cap
options.B: The external wall power plug
options.C: The claw or drive mechanism
options.D: The digital display screen

explanation: Correct! The drive mechanism (or claw) locks onto the plunger and slowly advances it to deliver the exact dose. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of red blood cells (erythrocytes) in our body?

options.A: Releasing antibodies during an allergic reaction
options.B: Transporting oxygen to body tissues
options.C: Forming initial plugs to stop bleeding
options.D: Fighting off bacterial infections

explanation: Awesome! Red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, acting like tiny delivery vans that pick up oxygen in the lungs and drop it off all over the body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is checking the suction apparatus considered a critical step before beginning the intubation procedure?

options.A: To inflate the balloon cuff once the tube is in the trachea
options.B: To quickly clear vomit, blood, or secretions blocking the view
options.C: To measure the exact volume of air inside the patient's lungs
options.D: To deliver humidified oxygen straight down the breathing tube

explanation: Unforeseen fluids can instantly obscure the clinician's view of the vocal cords, making immediate suction essential for patient safety. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T16#GNS213_U2_T16_h2)

question: A study shows that patients with higher anxiety report higher pain levels. Why can the researcher NOT claim that anxiety causes the pain?

options.A: Because anxiety is an experimental variable
options.B: Because pain cannot be measured using numerical scales
options.C: Because the sample size was likely too small to matter
options.D: Because correlational designs do not test cause and effect

explanation: Spot on! Finding a connection between two things just shows they move together; it doesn't prove one actually caused the other. Correlation is not causation! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T8#GNS224_U1_T8_h3)

question: A patient on a harsh detox diet feels dizzy, weak, and has muscle cramps. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Sudden overproduction of essential vitamins in the liver
options.B: Rapid cleansing of toxins from the central nervous system
options.C: Electrolyte imbalances and severe caloric depletion
options.D: Increased metabolic efficiency burning excess fat stores

explanation: Starving the body of proper food and water messes up vital minerals (electrolytes) like sodium and potassium, causing weakness and cramps. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h4)

question: What makes exercising managerial authority particularly tricky in many Nigerian healthcare facilities?

options.A: The complete absence of any formal organizational charts or job descriptions
options.B: Navigating severe resource shortages alongside rigid bureaucratic and traditional structures
options.C: A total lack of interaction between doctors and nursing personnel
options.D: Federal laws that prohibit registered nurses from supervising support staff

explanation: Nigerian nurse managers do amazing work balancing strict rules, cultural respect, and tough resource shortages every single day. True heroes! [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h7)

question: How does a high calorie diet differ from a standard maintenance diet?

options.A: It relies solely on liquid vitamin supplements
options.B: It focuses on energy density rather than food restriction
options.C: It restricts total daily fluid volume
options.D: It eliminates all complex carbohydrates

explanation: While standard diets often focus on portion control, high calorie diets aim to pack the maximum amount of energy into manageable food portions. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h1)

question: What is the very first step in the adult Chain of Survival?

options.A: Early recognition and prevention
options.B: Giving emergency medications
options.C: Advanced airway placement
options.D: Starting mouth-to-mouth rescue breathing

explanation: Spotting danger signs early helps prevent cardiac arrest before it even happens. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is the main job of bile when it comes to digesting fats?

options.A: Neutralizing stomach acid in the stomach lumen
options.B: Absorbing cholesterol directly into the bloodstream
options.C: Emulsifying large fat droplets into smaller pieces
options.D: Chemically breaking down fatty acids into simple sugars

explanation: Think of bile as natural dish soap for your food! It breaks big globs of fat into tiny droplets so digestive enzymes can easily mix in and finish the job. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h6)

question: How do chronic conditions like sickle cell anemia affect a woman during labour?

options.A: They guarantee that labour will start exactly two weeks early
options.B: They completely stop the mother from feeling uterine contractions
options.C: They severely strain maternal organs during the physical stress of childbirth
options.D: They prevent the baby from ever crying after birth

explanation: Labour is like running a marathon for the body! Conditions like sickle cell make it harder for the mother's organs to handle that heavy physical stress. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h2)

question: A patient comes in after a clandestine abortion with a high fever, smelly vaginal discharge, and lower tummy pain. What is the most likely problem?

options.A: Normal postpartum involution
options.B: Pelvic inflammatory sepsis
options.C: Uncomplicated uterine atony
options.D: Primary ovarian hyperstimulation

explanation: Fever plus foul-smelling discharge is a red flag for infection. Unsterile instruments easily introduce bacteria right into the uterus, leading quickly to pelvic sepsis. Great clinical spotting! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h2)

question: When is the correct time to document that you have given a medication?

options.A: Before walking into the patient's room to prepare the drugs
options.B: Immediately after giving the medication to the patient
options.C: At the very end of the working shift before going home
options.D: Whenever another colleague reminds you to update the chart

explanation: Chart right away after administration! Doing it immediately prevents accidental double-dosing and keeps the patient's records accurate. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T1#GNS125_U4_T1_h7)

question: A patient's IV arm feels tight, looks swollen, and feels cool to the touch. What complication has likely happened?

options.A: Infiltration
options.B: Phlebitis
options.C: Systemic infection
options.D: Air embolism

explanation: When IV fluids leak out into the surrounding skin tissue instead of the vein, we call it infiltration. The skin will look pale, swollen, and feel cool. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h8)

question: A patient develops a fever, cough, and shortness of breath five days after being admitted to the surgical ward for a knee replacement. How is this infection classified?

options.A: Hospital-acquired pneumonia
options.B: Aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Community-acquired pneumonia
options.D: Primary acute bronchitis

explanation: Any pneumonia symptoms appearing 48 hours or longer after a patient is admitted to a healthcare facility are classified as hospital-acquired or nosocomial pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T6#GNS213_U2_T6_h2)

question: A patient is complaining of terrible menstrual cramps. Which chemical messenger is mostly to blame for these strong uterine contractions?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Prostaglandins

explanation: Blame the prostaglandins! When the endometrium releases these chemicals, they make the uterine muscles squeeze tightly, causing those painful cramps (dysmenorrhea). [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h6)

question: In infection control, what do we mean by a 'reservoir'?

options.A: The natural home where a microorganism lives and multiplies
options.B: The method by which a germ travels through the air
options.C: An opening where germs leave the human body
options.D: A person who is vulnerable to catching a disease

explanation: Think of a reservoir as a cozy hangout spot for germs—it could be a human, an animal, soil, or even equipment where they live and grow. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h3)

question: Which scenario is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

options.A: Getting infected with malaria from a mosquito bite during the rainy season
options.B: Catching a cold after touching a shared pen that an infected coworker used
options.C: Developing a wound infection from direct contact with a draining sore
options.D: Inhaling large respiratory droplets expelled by someone coughing nearby

explanation: The shared pen acts as a fomite, transferring the virus indirectly from the coworker's hand to the new host's hand. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why must strict sterile technique be used when handling parenteral nutrition (IV feeding) lines?

options.A: Sterile technique stops the plastic from melting
options.B: Central lines connect to the digestive tract
options.C: The high nutrient content breeds bacteria fast
options.D: IV solutions contain live active bacteria

explanation: That's correct! Because these IV solutions are packed with sugars and proteins, germs love to grow in them, risking serious infection. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h6)

question: As a nursing student, how should you easily tell the difference between 'morbidity' and 'mortality'?

options.A: Morbidity is a statistic while mortality is a clinical diagnosis
options.B: Morbidity refers to illness while mortality refers to death
options.C: Morbidity affects only infants while mortality affects mothers
options.D: Morbidity is always preventable while mortality is inevitable

explanation: Think of it this way: morbidity means being sick or having health complications, while mortality simply means death. Simple and clear! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h1)

question: Why are flashing lights and visual alert systems helpful for patients with severe hearing loss?

options.A: They provide visual warnings for home safety hazards that sounds might miss
options.B: Flashing lights help regenerate damaged hair cells inside the inner ear
options.C: They replace the need for regular hearing aid battery replacements
options.D: Bright lights automatically adjust the volume of household televisions

explanation: Brilliant! Since they might miss audio cues, flashing lights for doorbells or smoke alarms help keep them safe at home. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T7#GNS324_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why shouldn't you squeeze a manual resuscitator bag way too hard during ventilation?

options.A: It causes the oxygen tank to explode
options.B: It instantly damages the heart muscle
options.C: It prevents carbon dioxide from leaving the room
options.D: It can force air into the stomach and cause vomiting

explanation: Squeezing too hard opens up the pathway to the stomach. Filling the stomach with air is a quick ticket to vomiting and aspiration—definitely something we want to avoid! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h3)

question: Why do community health nurses need to know basic epidemiological terms?

options.A: To diagnose rare surgical conditions in the emergency room
options.B: To track illnesses and plan local health outreaches effectively
options.C: To calculate hospital building construction costs
options.D: To prescribe complex medications without consulting doctors

explanation: Spotting disease trends helps you plan amazing, targeted health outreaches for your community. You're building skills that save real lives! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of standardizing clinical routines in nursing?

options.A: To eliminate the need for critical thinking during emergencies
options.B: To ensure all patients are discharged on the exact same day
options.C: To make nursing documentation take twice as long to complete
options.D: To reduce dangerous clinical variation and lower the risk of error

explanation: Standardization helps everyone follow safe, proven steps so patient care stays consistent and secure. [learn more](GST319_U5_T4#GST319_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the most serious and permanent complication of untreated onchocerciasis?

options.A: Blindness
options.B: Paraplegia
options.C: Deafness
options.D: Kidney failure

explanation: Long-term eye inflammation from dying microfilariae eventually scars the eye tissue, leading to irreversible river blindness if left untreated. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding pelvic rest after an MVA?

options.A: Avoid eating solid food for at least 48 hours post-procedure
options.B: Keep taking vaginal douches daily to clean out old blood
options.C: Exercise strenuously starting the very next morning
options.D: Avoid sexual intercourse and tampons for about two weeks

explanation: To prevent bacteria from entering the healing cervix and causing an infection, patients are advised against putting anything in the vagina for two weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h6)

question: What is a major reason why children end up roaming the streets in many communities?

options.A: Excessive participation in organized school sports
options.B: Severe poverty and financial hardship at home
options.C: Strict adherence to traditional cultural values
options.D: Overabundance of free government-provided housing

explanation: Spot on. Extreme financial hardship at home often forces families to send children out to find money, leaving them exposed and vulnerable on the streets. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h2)

question: A mother wants to mark her newborn baby for protection. How should the nurse best handle this counseling?

options.A: Threaten to call security if she attempts the procedure
options.B: Perform the cuts safely using hospital surgical blades
options.C: Explain infection risks gently and suggest safer alternatives
options.D: Ignore the conversation because it is a private family matter

explanation: That's brilliant nursing! Respectful education bridges cultural beliefs with health safety without pushing the client away. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h6)

question: A patient asks why they shouldn't watch TV in bed. What is the best nursing explanation?

options.A: It permanently ruins the mattress springs through excessive vibration.
options.B: Television screens emit toxic gases that destroy melatonin receptors.
options.C: It trains your brain to associate the bed with wakefulness rather than sleep.
options.D: Watching television lowers your body temperature below safe levels.

explanation: We want your brain to look at the bed and immediately think 'sleep!', not 'let's watch movies or scroll Instagram.' Keeping screens out of bed protects that crucial mental link. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h8)

question: How can outsourcing and PPPs make daily nursing work a bit tricky?

options.A: By ensuring all healthcare workers are employed directly by the government
options.B: By introducing mixed staffing models that can cause communication gaps and confusion
options.C: By eliminating any possibility of professional disagreement among staff
options.D: By completely removing the need for interprofessional collaboration in hospitals

explanation: When some workers are government staff and others belong to a private vendor, teamwork and communication can sometimes get tangled. [learn more](GST322_U4_T5#GST322_U4_T5_h8)

question: What is the main target tissue of the somatic nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine glands
options.B: Skeletal muscle
options.C: Smooth muscle
options.D: Cardiac muscle

explanation: Correct! The somatic system controls your voluntary movements by talking directly to your skeletal muscles. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts exposed healthy people
options.B: Quarantine is permanent, while isolation lasts for only a few hours
options.C: Isolation is for animals, while quarantine is strictly for human patients
options.D: Quarantine uses medications, while isolation only uses physical barriers

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation keeps already sick people away from others. Quarantine keeps healthy people who were exposed to a germ apart, just in case they develop symptoms later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h6)

question: What is a practical way to evaluate if a community mental health campaign was successful?

options.A: Counting how many flyers were thrown into the dustbin
options.B: Asking international donors how they feel from abroad
options.C: Checking if clinic attendance for early mental health support increased
options.D: Closing down the local health center to test community resilience

explanation: Tracking behavioral shifts, such as increased early clinic visits, shows whether awareness campaigns successfully translated into actual health-seeking actions. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a clinic or hospital?

options.A: To generate huge profits for hospital management
options.B: To store expired medications safely before disposal
options.C: To maintain a continuous and steady supply of essential drugs
options.D: To provide free medical treatment to all citizens

explanation: You've got this! The whole point of a DRF is to make sure essential medicines never run out. Money collected from sales is used right away to buy fresh stock. Simple and effective! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why is swelling of the kidney drainage system (hydronephrosis) more common on the right side during pregnancy?

options.A: The right renal artery has a higher pressure than the left.
options.B: The pregnant uterus tilts and compresses the right ureter more.
options.C: The right kidney is anatomically larger than the left kidney.
options.D: Progesterone receptors are concentrated only in the right ureter.

explanation: The growing uterus tends to lean to the right, putting extra pressure on the right ureter. Small details like this make you a sharp clinical nurse! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T5#GNS121_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why would a doctor order a skin KOH (potassium hydroxide) test?

options.A: To dissolve skin keratin and check for fungal elements under a microscope
options.B: To test for immediate severe allergic reactions to local anesthetic drugs
options.C: To measure the exact electrical resistance across a thickened skin plaque
options.D: To destroy abnormal surface cells using controlled freezing temperatures

explanation: Spot on! The KOH solution melts away the tough skin keratin so any sneaky fungus or yeast hiding underneath becomes easy to see. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T6#GNS213_U5_T6_h4)

question: Why must a nurse pay attention to non-verbal cues like facial expressions during an assessment?

options.A: Patients may hide their true emotional distress behind polite words
options.B: Non-verbal cues are the only way to measure blood pressure accurately
options.C: Patients expect nurses to read their minds without asking questions
options.D: Hospital regulations require charting body language every hour

explanation: Exactly! People often say they are fine while their body language quietly reveals anxiety, pain, or fear. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness in pregnancy?

options.A: To eliminate the need for routine antenatal visits
options.B: To choose the exact time and date of labor
options.C: To remove delays in accessing emergency obstetric care
options.D: To guarantee a home delivery without any skilled staff

explanation: Planning ahead for transport and funds helps ensure a woman gets to the hospital fast if an emergency happens. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h8)

question: Which of these is assessed during a standard Mental Status Examination (MSE)?

options.A: Complete blood count and electrolyte levels
options.B: Electrocardiogram heart rhythm tracing
options.C: Surgical wound healing and drainage amount
options.D: Thought process and perceptual disturbances

explanation: During an MSE, we focus on psychological signs—like how the patient's thoughts flow, their mood, and if they are experiencing things like hallucinations. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which hormone keeps the uterus relaxed and quiet throughout most of pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prostaglandin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone is like a chill pill for the uterus, keeping the muscles relaxed until it's time to meet the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h3)

question: A patient who lost their job six months ago visits the clinic complaining of constant headaches and stomach aches with no clear medical cause. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: A rare genetic blood disorder
options.B: An acute bacterial infection
options.C: A reaction to routine childhood immunizations
options.D: Somatic symptoms of underlying psychological stress

explanation: Spot on! People facing job loss often express emotional distress through physical aches, known as somatic symptoms. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h2)

question: Where does the front part of the pituitary gland (anterior pituitary) come from during early development?

options.A: The bony depression of the sphenoid bone known as the sella turcica
options.B: Downward growth of neural tissue directly from the hypothalamus
options.C: An outpouching of the embryonic pharynx called Rathke's pouch
options.D: The mesodermal layer surrounding the developing brain structures

explanation: Rathke's pouch is a fascinating little pocket of tissue from the roof of the mouth that pinches off to form the glandular front part of your pituitary. Embryology can look tricky, but breaking it down makes it simple! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which group usually faces the hardest time moving to safety during an emergency evacuation?

options.A: Elderly individuals and people with disabilities
options.B: Young adults with personal cars
options.C: Trained rescue personnel
options.D: Government officials in the capital city

explanation: Older people and those with physical challenges often struggle to move quickly or hear alerts during a rush. Every little bit of practice counts! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T11#GNS315_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why do many Nigerian families prefer home health care for their sick relatives?

options.A: To completely avoid paying any hospital bills
options.B: To comply with mandatory national health insurance rules
options.C: To access advanced surgical theaters at home
options.D: To bypass long hospital queues and get personal attention

explanation: Spot on! Families love home care because it helps them dodge long hospital waits and gives their loved one undivided attention. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h1)

question: How does making modern contraception easy for everyone to get help lower maternal death rates?

options.A: By shortening the normal physiological gestation period for women
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for emergency obstetric departments
options.C: By preventing all forms of sexually transmitted bacterial infections
options.D: By reducing the incidence of unintended pregnancies and unsafe abortions

explanation: Prevention is key! When people can easily access contraception, unplanned pregnancies drop, which means fewer people resort to dangerous, life-threatening unsafe abortions. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h6)

question: In polyvalent nursing, what does giving 'holistic care' mean?

options.A: Focusing strictly on medication administration schedules
options.B: Prioritizing hospital administrative rules over patients
options.C: Treating only the specific disease diagnosed by a doctor
options.D: Looking at the whole person including body and mind

explanation: Exactly! Holistic care means looking at the patient as a complete human being—body, mind, and spirit—rather than just focusing on a single symptom. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: In the context of vulnerable families, what is 'property grabbing'?

options.A: Community members stealing food donations meant for orphans
options.B: Relatives seizing land and belongings after a parent dies
options.C: The government confiscating hospital records of deceased patients
options.D: Banks freezing accounts belonging to children under age eighteen

explanation: Property grabbing happens when greedy relatives unlawfully chase away a grieving widow and her children to take over their home and properties. It's a harsh reality nurses should be aware of to guide families. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T2#GNS225_U5_T2_h4)

question: Why do women who have undergone infibulation frequently suffer from recurrent urinary tract infections?

options.A: Urine pools behind the scar tissue and narrow opening, promoting bacterial growth.
options.B: Frequent catheterization is required for basic hygiene.
options.C: The procedure permanently destroys the kidneys' ability to filter waste.
options.D: Hormonal imbalances alter the natural pH of the bladder.

explanation: A constricted or partially blocked urinary outlet prevents complete bladder emptying, leaving residual urine that easily harbors bacteria. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is considered the absolute cornerstone of youth-friendly healthcare?

options.A: Formal hospital uniforms
options.B: Expensive equipment
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Strict parental control

explanation: Guarantees of privacy and confidentiality are essential to make young people feel safe enough to share personal health details. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h7)

question: Which of these is a common trap to avoid when writing a research question?

options.A: Consulting clinical nurses before finalizing the topic
options.B: Ensuring the question uses simple, clear vocabulary
options.C: Making the question far too broad to manage
options.D: Checking the question against the PICOT framework

explanation: It's easy to want to solve all the world's problems at once! But keeping your question focused stops you from getting overwhelmed with too much data. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is a true red-light contraindication for giving a vaccine?

options.A: A history of severe allergic reaction to a previous dose
options.B: A mild cold with a low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees
options.C: A family history of minor skin rashes
options.D: Current recovery from mild diarrhea at home

explanation: If a patient had a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) before, giving another dose is a huge safety risk. Always check past records! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h3)

question: When taking a family history, which relatives are most important to include?

options.A: Coworkers and roommates
options.B: Neighbors and close family friends
options.C: Distant cousins and great-great-grandparents
options.D: Immediate family members like parents, siblings, and children

explanation: Immediate family members share the closest genetic link, making their health history most relevant for hereditary risks. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T2#GNS123_U2_T2_h5)

question: How do antibiotics used in agriculture often end up in humans?

options.A: Through the food chain from livestock consumption
options.B: By drinking purified bottled water from wells
options.C: Through direct injection of vaccines in schools
options.D: By airborne dust blowing directly into city hospitals

explanation: When farm animals are given antibiotics, resistant germs can develop in them and pass on to humans through meat handling or consumption. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h5)

question: How should you document an adverse event in the patient's clinical chart?

options.A: Include notes about the hospital management being careless
options.B: Record objective clinical findings and nursing interventions clearly
options.C: Write down personal opinions about which coworker made the mistake
options.D: Avoid mentioning the event entirely to prevent patient anxiety

explanation: Keep your charting strictly factual! Write down only what you see, assess, and do for the patient. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h3)

question: Why should a nurse be concerned if a patient breaks a bone easily from just a minor bump or fall?

options.A: It raises suspicion for underlying bone weakness or metabolic bone disease
options.B: It confirms the patient has normal bone mineral density
options.C: It indicates that the patient has a severe muscular infection
options.D: It proves the patient engages in professional contact sports

explanation: Spot-on! Bones shouldn't break from minor bumps. This is a huge warning sign for conditions like osteoporosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h5)

question: An older adult in a care home suddenly becomes confused today, even though they are usually clear-headed. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Normal aging process
options.B: A developing infection
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: A high-protein diet

explanation: Great clinical instinct! In older adults, a sudden change in mental state or confusion is often the very first clue that an infection like a UTI is brewing. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h5)

question: What does the popular research acronym IMRAD stand for?

options.A: Inquiry, Materials, Recording, And Documentation
options.B: Introduction, Methods, Results, And Discussion
options.C: Investigation, Measurement, Review, And Data
options.D: Interpretation, Management, Research, And Draft

explanation: Think IMRAD: Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It is the golden standard structure for organizing research papers! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h2)

question: What is one of the most common ways cultural stigma affects people with mental health challenges?

options.A: Hospitals receive extra funding for psychiatric care
options.B: Individuals hide their symptoms and avoid seeking professional help
options.C: Families immediately bring patients to the clinic
options.D: Community members openly discuss their emotions

explanation: Stigma breeds fear and shame, making people suffer in silence rather than risk being judged by others. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is a classic example of indirect transmission via a fomite?

options.A: Catching an infection after touching a contaminated door handle
options.B: Getting malaria from a mosquito bite
options.C: Contracting a sexually transmitted infection through direct contact
options.D: Inhaling large droplets expelled during a close-range sneeze

explanation: A 'fomite' is just a fancy word for any non-living object—like a door handle, phone, or pen—that carries germs from one person to another. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary direction of time in a prospective research design?

options.A: Moving backward from the present into the past
options.B: Comparing two different time periods in history
options.C: Moving forward from the present into the future
options.D: Examining past medical records for current outcomes

explanation: Prospective studies are designed to follow participants forward in time to observe future outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h1)

question: What usually happens to uterine fibroids after a woman goes through menopause?

options.A: They calcify and cause acute infections
options.B: They rapidly grow larger and turn malignant
options.C: They multiply and spread to other organs
options.D: They usually shrink due to lower hormone levels

explanation: Because fibroids love estrogen and progesterone, they naturally shrink when hormone production drops after menopause. Nature's way of helping out! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h2)

question: Which hormones are primarily released by the body during an acute stress response?

options.A: Oxytocin and melatonin
options.B: Adrenaline and cortisol
options.C: Insulin and glucagon
options.D: Thyroid and estrogen

explanation: These major stress hormones prepare the body instantly to confront danger or run away from it. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h2)

question: Why is advocacy so important in primary health care, way beyond just giving treatments?

options.A: It directly cures infectious diseases without medication
options.B: It guarantees immediate government funding for hospitals
options.C: It replaces the need for community health workers
options.D: It addresses systemic barriers that limit healthcare access

explanation: Great thinking! Handing out medications doesn't fix big problems like poverty or bad roads to the clinic. Advocacy tackles those root barriers that keep people from getting care. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why does a drop in immunization coverage pose a major danger to a community?

options.A: It leads to severe outbreaks of preventable diseases
options.B: It causes immediate antibiotic resistance in infants
options.C: It increases the cost of treating chronic genetic disorders
options.D: It permanently ruins the cold chain storage equipment

explanation: When too many children miss their shots, community immunity falls, allowing dangerous infections to return and spread rapidly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h1)

question: Why do patients who experience harmful traditional practices often keep it a secret from healthcare workers?

options.A: Because modern medical treatments cannot cure traditional injuries
options.B: They are usually unaware that their physical symptoms are abnormal
options.C: Fear of social backlash, punishment, or betraying family customs
options.D: Hospitals explicitly forbid patients from discussing cultural events

explanation: You're doing great! Survivors often stay quiet because they are afraid of what their community might say or do to their families. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T1#GNS312_U1_T1_h6)

question: A nurse receives a batch of donated nutrition teaching materials from an NGO. What is the best way to use them?

options.A: Give them all to private doctors in the city center
options.B: Integrate them into daily antenatal health talks and clinic education
options.C: Throw them away because they did not come from the ministry
options.D: Lock them away in a drawer until the NGO supervisor visits

explanation: Brilliant! Donated materials are most helpful when put straight into daily clinic activities like antenatal talks to educate mothers. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why are rats, mice, and insects so dangerous around a kitchen?

options.A: They make food lose its vitamins too quickly
options.B: They make annoying noises that disturb staff and guests
options.C: They eat too much food and increase restaurant bills
options.D: They carry and spread dangerous germs on their bodies and waste

explanation: Pests carry loads of bacteria, viruses, and parasites. When they crawl over surfaces, they leave behind invisible pathogens that can make people sick. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h6)

question: Which virus is the most common cause of severe, watery diarrhoea in babies?

options.A: Influenza virus
options.B: Varicella zoster
options.C: Hepatitis A
options.D: Rotavirus

explanation: Rotavirus is well-known as the leading viral culprit behind severe dehydrating diarrhoea in infants worldwide. Vaccination has been a game-changer here! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h2)

question: A nurse manager creates a ward schedule that requires double the current nursing staff, ignoring the hospital budget. Which principle of planning was violated?

options.A: Continuity
options.B: Flexibility
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Secrecy

explanation: Feasibility means a plan must be realistic and work within actual available resources like budgets and staff numbers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a known complication of bone fractures?

options.A: Fat embolism syndrome affecting the lungs
options.B: Compartment syndrome due to increased tissue pressure
options.C: Osteomyelitis resulting from a bone infection
options.D: Uncontrolled high blood sugar or type 1 diabetes

explanation: You've got it! Diabetes is an endocrine condition, not a direct complication of breaking a bone. The others (fat emboli, infections, and compartment syndrome) are major risks we watch out for. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T4#GNS112_U7_T4_h6)

question: What does healthcare data access primarily allow authorized medical personnel to do?

options.A: Retrieve, view, and utilize patient information
options.B: Change hospital billing rates directly
options.C: Delete old patient records permanently
options.D: Share patient details publicly on social media

explanation: Data access gives clinicians the ability to pull up and use patient records to guide medical care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of disaster 'mitigation'?

options.A: Treating injured survivors in a hospital emergency room
options.B: Broadcasting breaking news of a collapsed building
options.C: Enforcing building codes in flood-prone areas
options.D: Distributing blankets to displaced families in a camp

explanation: Well done! Mitigation is all about taking action *before* disaster strikes to reduce risk and prevent harm—like making sure buildings can withstand floods. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the main goal of creating a "Just Culture" in a hospital?

options.A: To eliminate all forms of nursing accountability for clinical mistakes
options.B: To ensure that every person who makes a mistake is fired immediately
options.C: To protect the hospital administration from medical malpractice lawsuits
options.D: To encourage honest reporting of errors without the immediate fear of punishment

explanation: Brilliant! A Just Culture means we can speak up honestly when things go wrong without shaking in our boots, so the whole team can learn and fix the system. [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h4)

question: What type of data is best displayed using a bar chart?

options.A: Individual patient DNA sequences
options.B: Raw unorganized audio
options.C: Categorical data
options.D: Continuous time data

explanation: Bar charts are specifically designed to show and compare distinct groups or categories of information. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h1)

question: As a nurse, what is the best first step before handing out a sleeping pill?

options.A: Checking the patient's visual acuity in bright sunlight
options.B: Administering a cup of strong coffee to test drug interactions
options.C: Requiring the patient to sign a legal release form
options.D: Assessing the underlying cause of insomnia and trying sleep hygiene measures

explanation: Always check why they can't sleep and try natural comfort tips first before reaching straight for the prescription pad! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T1#GNS223_U6_T1_h7)

question: When times are hard and inflation is high, what do many patients do regarding out-of-pocket healthcare costs?

options.A: They purchase extra quantities of prescription drugs for storage
options.B: They demand immediate hospital admission for minor symptoms
options.C: They visit private specialist clinics more frequently for routine checkups
options.D: They delay seeking medical care until their condition becomes a severe emergency

explanation: When money is tight, people often wait until they are extremely sick before coming to the hospital, which makes treatment much harder. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which dressing works best for a wound that has heavy bleeding or fluid drainage?

options.A: Dry gauze pad
options.B: Transparent film
options.C: Hydrocolloid wafer
options.D: Alginate dressing

explanation: Alginates come from seaweed and are superstars at soaking up lots of fluid while turning into a soft gel that keeps the wound bed happy. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is a common trap to avoid when designing a conceptual framework?

options.A: Sharing the research design with student nurses
options.B: Writing the framework on a white sheet of paper
options.C: Making the framework too complex and cluttered
options.D: Using too few words in the title of the study

explanation: Don't try to cram every single idea in the universe into one diagram! Keep it clean, simple, and testable. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h8)

question: How does community stigma often affect families living with an HIV-positive member?

options.A: It forces local health clinics to provide free housing
options.B: It causes families to isolate themselves from others
options.C: It encourages families to seek out more social groups
options.D: It improves the family's financial stability over time

explanation: Exactly. Fear of unfair judgment and discrimination can make households withdraw from friends and community activities out of worry. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h2)

question: Days after surviving a flood, a patient is restless, has a racing heart, and worries constantly. What is the best way to describe this?

options.A: Anxiety and panic
options.B: Depressive symptoms
options.C: Somatization
options.D: Acute stress reaction

explanation: Spot on! Constant worry, a restless body, and a fast heartbeat are classic signs of anxiety and panic following a scary crisis event. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h2)

question: Which agency coordinates national disaster management in Nigeria?

options.A: Nigerian Union_of Journalists
options.B: Federal Road Safety Corps exclusively
options.C: National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA)
options.D: National Youth Service Corps

explanation: You nailed it! NEMA is the main federal body that handles disaster planning and response across Nigeria. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h6)

question: A nurse is getting ready to apply a new fentanyl pain patch to a patient. What important step must be done first?

options.A: Cover the new patch completely with airtight plastic wrap
options.B: Scrub the application site aggressively with surgical soap
options.C: Remove the previous transdermal patch from the patient's skin
options.D: Warm the new patch over a flame to activate the chemicals

explanation: Always take off the old patch before putting on a new one! Leaving the old patch on can cause a dangerous, life-threatening drug overdose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h5)

question: How has the traditional Almajiri system in some parts of Nigeria unfortunately contributed to street children numbers?

options.A: Extreme poverty has stripped away structural support, leaving pupils to beg for survival
options.B: Religious teachers train children specifically to migrate to foreign countries
options.C: The government mandates that all Quranic students live exclusively outdoors
options.D: Boarding facilities for students are overfunded and turn children away

explanation: You're doing great. When the system lacks enough food and shelter resources, young students are left with no choice but to beg on the streets to eat. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T3#GNS225_U5_T3_h2)

question: A patient on a tight budget wants a cheap, local source of protein. What should you recommend?

options.A: Imported salmon fillets
options.B: Processed energy drinks
options.C: Beans and cowpeas
options.D: Refined white sugar

explanation: Local beans and cowpeas are fantastic, pocket-friendly powerhouses of plant-based protein right here in Nigeria! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h3)

question: Which method do nurses usually use to gather health facts directly from a community?

options.A: Conducting home visits and community dialogues
options.B: Waiting for international health organizations to send reports
options.C: Consulting only with the federal minister of health
options.D: Reviewing international stock market trends

explanation: Great choice! Going directly into the community through visits and talks gives nurses a clear picture of real health conditions. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is one exciting benefit expected from future voice-activated documentation tools?

options.A: Allowing nurses to speak clinical notes while performing procedures
options.B: Replacing the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: Automatically bathing patients using robotic spray systems
options.D: Eliminating all hospital noise during the night shift

explanation: Brilliant! Voice tech aims to save us time by letting us dictate our notes hands-free while we work. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h7)

question: A student nurse is getting ready to irrigate an eye. Which action means they need a quick correction?

options.A: Placing a waterproof towel and a kidney basin under the cheek
options.B: Encouraging the patient to blink periodically during the wash
options.C: Resting fingers directly upon the patient's eyeball to hold it open
options.D: Holding the irrigation tubing about one inch away from the eye

explanation: Ouch! Always rest your fingers on the bony cheekbone or forehead, never directly on the eyeball, to prevent accidental pressure injury. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T12#GNS122_U1_T12_h5)

question: A patient in the intensive care unit is being evaluated for potential brain death. Which test is routinely used to confirm this?

options.A: Electroencephalography
options.B: Lumbar puncture
options.C: Barium swallow study
options.D: Electromyography

explanation: When doctors need to check for remaining brain activity in severe cases, a completely flatline EEG (cerebral silence) helps confirm brain death. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h2)

question: In simple terms, what does endocrine 'hyposecretion' mean?

options.A: Hormones are destroyed in the bloodstream
options.B: A gland produces too little of a hormone
options.C: A gland produces too much of a hormone
options.D: Target organs completely reject hormones

explanation: You've got this! 'Hypo-' always means under or low. So hyposecretion just means the gland isn't making enough hormone. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h1)

question: How do prospective study findings directly benefit frontline nurses working in clinical wards?

options.A: By providing historical background on ancient medical discoveries
options.B: By eliminating the need for patient assessments during night shifts
options.C: By replacing all bedside charting with automated computer algorithms
options.D: By helping identify high-risk patients early so preventative nursing care can be applied

explanation: Prospective research uncovers risk factors that frontline nurses use to spot vulnerable patients and prevent adverse hospital events. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h7)

question: What is the main difference between airborne and droplet transmission?

options.A: Droplet particles can travel for miles across different cities
options.B: Droplet transmission requires a mosquito bite to start working
options.C: Airborne droplet nuclei stay suspended in the air much longer
options.D: Airborne particles only spread through contaminated drinking water

explanation: Airborne transmission involves tiny particles that stay in the air and travel far, whereas large droplets quickly fall to the ground. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why do community health nurses need to be very independent in their practice?

options.A: They possess sole authority to prescribe major surgical procedures
options.B: They operate completely isolated from any oversight or guidelines
options.C: They frequently make independent clinical judgments during home visits
options.D: They manage entire regional hospitals without assistance

explanation: Spot on! When you're out doing home visits or working in rural outposts, you won't always have a doctor right beside you, so you'll trust your training to make sharp, independent choices. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h2)

question: A nurse manager needs to buy daily supplies of syringes and gauze. Under which budget category do these routine expenses fall?

options.A: Investment budget
options.B: Operating budget
options.C: Capital budget
options.D: Construction budget

explanation: Routine, day-to-day operational costs like medical supplies and staff salaries are managed through the operating budget. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is a red-flag sign of a severe allergic reaction that needs instant emergency help?

options.A: Sudden facial swelling and difficulty breathing
options.B: Faint drowsiness after taking a nighttime sedative
options.C: Slight urine discoloration from a vitamin supplement
options.D: Mild dry mouth lasting for two hours

explanation: Trouble breathing and swollen lips mean anaphylaxis. That is an all-hands-on-deck emergency in the ward! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h5)

question: A community insists that physical inactivity is not a problem for them at all. As a nurse, what should you do first?

options.A: Launch an intensive gym membership subsidy program
options.B: Close local food markets that sell processed snacks
options.C: Penalize community leaders for refusing to exercise
options.D: Raise awareness and build local recognition of the issue

explanation: Correct! When a community is in denial, jumping straight into action programs won't work. You have to start by building awareness of the issue first. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h3)

question: Which statement best captures the dimensional approach to mental health?

options.A: It measures symptom severity along a continuous spectrum
options.B: It ignores mild symptoms in favor of severe crises
options.C: It assigns every patient a rigid, permanent label
options.D: It relies solely on blood tests and imaging results

explanation: Instead of a simple yes-or-no box, the dimensional approach looks at how mild, moderate, or severe a client's symptoms are. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is another name for compact bone tissue?

options.A: Cancellous bone
options.B: Medullary bone
options.C: Trabecular bone
options.D: Cortical bone

explanation: Compact bone is also called cortical bone because it forms the hard outer cortex of bones. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h1)

question: How many primary lobes make up the glandular tissue of a human breast?

options.A: 2 to 5

explanation: A mature human breast typically contains 15 to 20 glandular lobes arranged radially around the nipple. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h3)

question: Which dimension of quality care ensures that clinical treatments are based on proven scientific guidelines?

options.A: Safety
options.B: Accessibility
options.C: Acceptability
options.D: Effectiveness

explanation: Brilliant! Effectiveness focuses on using evidence-based practices so that our nursing interventions actually achieve the best health outcomes for the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T4#GNS312_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of doing a community risk assessment?

options.A: Punishing communities that fail to follow sanitation laws
options.B: Reducing the total number of practicing nurses in a state
options.C: Preventing illness and health outbreaks before they occur
options.D: Generating revenue for private commercial pharmacies

explanation: Prevention is our superpower in public health! Finding risks early helps us stop sickness before it even starts. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a patient's sting site is developing a bacterial infection days later?

options.A: Spreading erythema, warmth, and purulent discharge at the site days later
options.B: Immediate localized pain and minor itching right after the sting
options.C: Clear fluid blisters that form and heal within twenty-four hours

question: What does the systolic blood pressure reading measure?

question: What does the acronym ADL stand for in healthcare?

question: What harmless side effect of oral iron supplements should you warn parents about?

question: A patient has an issue with making and circulating cerebrospinal fluid in the brain. Which cells are directly involved?

question: Why must you always keep a patient's culture and pocket (financial status) in mind when giving dietary advice?

question: Which of these symptoms means a food handler needs to step away from work right away?

question: Why is it tricky to use a stethoscope when a patient is lying on a very soft home bed?

question: A doctor dismisses your drug dose warning with sarcasm. What should you do next as an assertive nurse?

question: What are two major health risks associated with early unprotected sexual intercourse in adolescents?

question: Why does a hospital ward have separate clean utility and dirty utility rooms?

question: How is true sputum different from ordinary saliva?

question: Why do patients sometimes feel tummy pain during the early stage of this infection?

question: Why should community and home care nurses pay close attention to a patient's culture and home life?

question: If a patient keeps getting discharged and readmitted because there are no local clinics to support them, what historical issue does this show?

question: Which breathing sound tells you right away that a patient has an upper airway obstruction?

question: What happens when different tiers of government fail to coordinate their healthcare efforts?

question: How should a nurse properly perform a whisper test to check a patient's hearing?

question: How does a nurse's role shift when a patient moves from Tier 3 up to Tier 4?

question: Which of these is NOT a common complication of unmanaged maternal distress?

question: How does good family nutrition directly help a patient managing HIV?

question: Why is it helpful for nurses to understand basic economic trends?

question: Why does the body slow down digestion during pregnancy?

question: A 10-week-old baby is brought for immunizations, but currently has a high fever and a bad cough. What should you do?

explanation: Giving a solid piece of food to someone who requires a pureed diet can lead to airway obstruction and aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h3)

question: What do we call the natural home where a germ lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: Infectious agent
options.B: Reservoir
options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Portal of entry

explanation: Think of a reservoir as the home sweet home for germs! It's where they hang out, multiply, and get ready before moving on to a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h1)

question: How long does a seizure need to last to be called 'status epilepticus'?

options.A: Longer than five minutes
options.B: At least one full hour
options.C: More than twenty-four hours
options.D: Exactly thirty seconds

explanation: Any seizure lasting past five minutes—or happening back-to-back without waking up—is an emergency called status epilepticus. Quick thinking is vital here! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h8)

question: What is the primary job of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4) in the body?

options.A: Regulating the baseline basal metabolic rate of body cells
options.B: Releasing emergency calcium from bones during muscle tetany
options.C: Triggering water reabsorption in the kidney collecting ducts
options.D: Lowering sudden spikes in blood glucose after carbohydrate intake

explanation: T3 and T4 act like your body's engine idle speed, controlling how fast your cells burn energy and use oxygen every day. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which communication channel works best when discussing sensitive personal health issues?

options.A: A large billboard placed on the highway
options.B: Interpersonal communication like counseling
options.C: An anonymous pamphlet dropped in the mail
options.D: A commercial broadcast on national television

explanation: Face-to-face counseling builds trust and allows for private, two-way chats. It's the gold standard for sensitive topics! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h5)

question: How does having a larger risk pool help a health insurance scheme?

options.A: It balances out the costs between healthy and sick members more effectively
options.B: It ensures that taxes are completely abolished
options.C: It removes the need for patients to ever visit a pharmacy
options.D: It allows the hospital to hire foreign doctors exclusively

explanation: The more healthy people join the pool, the easier it is to cover the medical bills of the few who fall sick. Safety truly lies in numbers! [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h3)

question: Which immediate complication happens when an instrument accidentally punctures the muscular wall of the uterus during a procedure?

options.A: Secondary amenorrhea
options.B: Cervical incompetence
options.C: Gestational trophoblastic disease
options.D: Uterine perforation

explanation: Uterine perforation occurs when sharp instruments or foreign objects poke a hole right through the wall of the uterus. It's a surgical emergency you'll want to watch out for during recovery! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T026#GNS226_U5_T026_h3)

question: Which body publishes the famous Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM)?

options.A: The American Psychiatric Association
options.B: The Global Nursing Council
options.C: The International Medical Association
options.D: The World Health Organization

explanation: The American Psychiatric Association develops and updates the DSM. Handy fact to keep tucked in your brain for exams! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why do teenage boys and girls need different nutritional care during puberty?

options.A: Girls stop growing in height much earlier than boys do.
options.B: Boys develop more lean muscle while girls accumulate more body fat.
options.C: Girls require virtually no extra protein during puberty.
options.D: Boys have higher vitamin requirements than any other demographic.

explanation: That's correct! Puberty hormones push boys to build more muscle and bone, while girls naturally store a bit more body fat to support future reproductive needs. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T6#GNS312_U3_T6_h1)

question: What is the best position for a woman past 20 weeks pregnant to prevent dizziness from lying flat?

options.A: In a prone position
options.B: Sitting upright with legs dangling
options.C: Flat on her back
options.D: Lateral recumbent position

explanation: Correct! Lying on her side takes the weight of the womb off the main blood vessels, keeping blood flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h5)

question: Why might a patient with acute leukemia have swollen, bleeding gums?

options.A: Abnormal white blood cells infiltrate and build up in the gum tissue
options.B: Excessive red blood cells cause high pressure in mouth capillaries
options.C: The patient forgot to brush their teeth for several weeks
options.D: Saliva production completely stops due to bone marrow failure

explanation: In certain leukemias, immature white blood cells crowd into soft tissues like the gums, causing them to swell and bleed easily. Keep up the good reading! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T3#GNS311_U2_T3_h3)

question: When we talk about environmental determinants of mental health, what are we mainly referring to?

options.A: The chemical balance inside the brain cells
options.B: Only the genetic code inherited from biological parents
options.C: Factors in a person's surroundings and living conditions
options.D: Purely random events that happen during old age

explanation: Think of environmental determinants as everything around a person—their home, neighborhood, and daily life experiences—that shapes how they feel and cope. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h1)

question: A patient with a bleeding duodenal ulcer will likely show which lab result?

options.A: Decreased serum creatinine
options.B: Elevated white blood cell count
options.C: High platelet count
options.D: Low hemoglobin and hematocrit

explanation: You nailed it! Bleeding from an ulcer means losing blood over time, which causes iron-deficiency anemia seen as low hemoglobin and hematocrit on a lab report. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T7#GNS213_U3_T7_h4)
